items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: Coridge asked the guy who was managing the band, named Vandenberg... He told me, 'Phil, how would you like to make about a month with Louis Jordan?' I said, 'Fine.' ... During that time, you played with Louis Jordan. Yes.

ctx.x: Anyway, you were talking about this cutting session with Louis Jordan and Lester Young. "Running Wild" and playing the Blues...

The Blues and another one they played. "Yes sir, that's my baby..." Those were about the two tunes they played. Les blowed so much horn on that thing, and Louis Jordan was running over that soprano... You know, the soprano is more piercing than the alto. So they got to running over that. So Les said, "The only way I'm gonna get him, I'm gonna slap-tongue him." Les could slap-tongue, and play the same thing slap-tonguing than he played ordinarily, which I never heard nobody do it but him. So that's why everybody…
